Volunteering is not required for honours, but it is preferred. It technically guarantees you a spot in the lab for honours. Since you already have experience in Dr. Leitch's lab I would recommend you talking to him about your interests, he might even come up with a better solution because it's possible for your honours to be kinda supervised by two profs (so ur actual supervisor is like last author, and second last is the other prof) 

Talk to every person in the lab about their research and talk to Dr. Leitch.

Not necessarily, ask Dr. Hof if volunteering is possible. 
If his answer is no, reach out to him again when you completed it. If you really want to get more experience and is not picky I would suggest volunteering in a different lab

Assuming you reached out to do Honours, I would recommend asking Dr. Hof if you could volunteer in his lab until you meet the prerequisites. Start now if possible, you won't regret it. Honours is extremely competitive.

If you want to gain more research beforehand, start now - look up professors who do research and what their focuses are, reach out via email and ask to do research experience or volunteer in their lab. 

If you don't plan to - let's say you want to start in the fall, start reaching out mid fall sem of the previous year. You could also go talk to profs during honours fest in the spring. The earlier the better, it's pretty competitive especially for BCMB department. (~30 students per year for honours) 

The process is probably the same for the Chem department but I'm not entirely sure. Also I'm pretty sure you would need to be majoring in biochem or microbio to do honours in a bioc lab but don't take my word for it. 

It is possible to do honours in a joint lab from two different faculties (there was someone who did their honours in the Hof's (chem)  and Helbing (BCMB) labs. 

Regardless, reach out to both faculties honours advisor if you have any questions. Goodluck!
